body:
Single-result source fetches create nested mapping iterators even without callbacks. Zero/one-variable results can be mapped by the existing HTTP-owning iterator.

This PR inlines only that callback-null path. Callback/multi-variable routes retain their original pipeline, preserving cancellation, disposal and callback Activity/AsyncLocal behavior.

### Benchmarks

The actual client/context/parser uses a deterministic in-memory HTTP handler; enumeration/disposal must complete synchronously. Arena replacement is outside measurement. Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, server/concurrent GC, four cores: default-GC timing, two-second warmup/shape, 32 windows of 4,096 fetches (512 at 32 sets). Baseline is the median of three launch medians; PR is one final launch. Ratios are time-separated observations.

Baseline `9a563e814f` C# matches main `706ec84ff2`. Measured candidate `d34d30a97c` matches this clean branch `4c82398203`; only Execution DLL/PDB changes in the identical consumer. Allocation runs use DATAS=0 and scoped executing-thread brackets.

| Variable sets / mode / callback | Baseline ns | PR ns | Time C/B | Baseline B/op | PR B/op | Alloc C/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0/indexed/off | 951.62 | 869.60 | 0.914 | 3304.19 | 3064.19* | 0.927* |
| 0/indexed/on | 1015.78 | 1007.25 | 0.992 | 3536.19 | 3560.19 | 1.007 |
| 1/indexed/off | 1007.91 | 899.74 | 0.893 | 3304.19 | 3064.19 | 0.927 |
| 1/indexed/on | 1063.05 | 1066.99 | 1.004 | 3536.19 | 3560.19 | 1.007 |
| 3/indexed/off | 2102.09 | 2259.29 | 1.075 | 4592.95 | 4616.95 | 1.005 |
| 3/indexed/on | 2205.10 | 2301.16 | 1.044 | 4824.95 | 4848.95 | 1.005 |
| 3/sequential/off | 2052.51 | 2106.18 | 1.026 | 5000.95 | 5024.95 | 1.005 |
| 3/sequential/on | 2265.33 | 2168.13 | 0.957 | 5232.95 | 5256.95 | 1.005 |
| 32/indexed/off | 14092.44 | 13114.17 | 0.931 | 17415.62 | 17439.62 | 1.001 |
| 32/indexed/on | 13900.95 | 14358.47 | 1.033 | 17647.62 | 17671.62 | 1.001 |

*Zero-set allocation is median-only: one window fails stability. One-set callback-off has exact -240 B scoped deltas/process-thread agreement in all 32 windows. Overall strict census remains failed; prior 48/1,048 B controls were separate. Default-HTTP total bytes remain unvalidated.

Release builds passed; fourteen direct/ambient frozen-baseline contracts and thirty-eight final client/batch cases passed.

[Method/HTTP evidence and limits](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/da82b30d00b3187bced84dfa649bf4b839ffe9c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/ITERATOR-SINGLE-TERMINAL-DECISION.md), [final timing and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/f92e09c2fd8a3e9b0e380edfb4287bd7390703c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/ITERATOR-SINGLE-TIMING-RESULT.md).

### HTTP revalidation

Fresh matched controls use the original frozen baseline `9a563e814f`, Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, default server/concurrent GC, four logical CPUs assigned to the gateway, 200 requests/s, 64 VUs and a fixed 4 ms source delay. Each fresh gateway gets 60 s warmup and 60 s measured traffic. One unchanged source process spans the balanced schedule: baseline, snapshot, enumeration, iterator, scope, baseline, scope, iterator, enumeration, snapshot, baseline. Only the candidate assembly/PDB differs from the frozen baseline.

All response, identity, request-accounting and CPU-counter checks passed, with zero errors or dropped starts. Every measured group completed 12,001 requests except enumeration run 2, which completed 12,000. CPU uses actual completions. No profiler ran; identical one-second state/process observations remained enabled. Native latency samples were checked against completion counts. Effective DATAS/heap count was not exposed and is not inferred.

| Run | CPU ms/request | CPU C/B, both surrounding controls | p95 ms | p99 ms | p99.9 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline-1 | 0.841673 | - | 10.296 | 12.653 | 19.686 |
| iterator-1 | 0.883965 | 1.0502–1.0660 | 10.162 | 12.871 | 21.231 |
| baseline-2 | 0.829226 | - | 9.834 | 11.829 | 16.288 |
| iterator-2 | 0.846516 | 1.0209–1.0478 | 10.058 | 11.962 | 16.146 |
| baseline-3 | 0.807881 | - | 10.050 | 12.369 | 20.243 |

Baseline CPU declined 4.01% across the campaign. Ratios show both surrounding controls without correcting away that drift. Requests and five-second blocks are dependent observations, not independent process launches. Matching-window OS/runtime checks validate the CPU counter; their bounds are not full-phase performance error bars. The comparison does not identify JIT or GC as a cause.

[Matched HTTP results, raw data and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/1e75ce82d3ec18dea4b2083272e0e946ab7c0872/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/SHARED-HTTP-REVALIDATION-RESULT.md).

### Verdict

**Abandoned because matched HTTP validation repeatedly increased CPU/request.** The first run used 5.02–6.60% more CPU than its two surrounding baselines; the reversed-order run used 2.09–4.78% more. The second increase remains adverse against both local controls even though it is close to the first, earlier baseline. Lower p95/p99 in some comparisons does not remove the repeated CPU cost.

Eligible fetches save 240 scoped bytes, while callback/multi-variable fallbacks add 24 B. Those microbenchmark savings do not justify the request-level CPU increase. The PR is closed; the prior time-separated +4.54% CPU observation is now supported by the matched runs.
title: [Fusion] Reduce allocations for single-result source fetches
